items.detail:
3 findings carried by reviewers against `content/wiki/model/z-ai-glm-4-7-flash.md`, batched into one job because they concern the same file. Each is stated below in the reviewing reviewer's own words. Fix every one, or say in `RESULT.md` which you did not and why — a finding you leave standing must keep its file.

### Cite the feed's own alias_target as the successor evidence, not just the name lineage

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260904-25-carry-1.md`.

The annotation asserts "the successor row" and supports it with vendor, tier, context and price — that is inference from naming, and it is the one judgment in the annotation that is not arithmetic. The same 2026-09-04 snapshot settles it outright and the annotation does not say so: the row `~z-ai/glm-flash-latest`, whose own description reads "This model always redirects to the latest model in the GLM Flash family", carries `alias_target: {"name":"Z.ai: GLM 5.3 Flash","slug":"z-ai/glm-5.3-flash"}`. That is OpenRouter declaring the current GLM Flash model in the feed itself. The next annotation on this row (one is due — the same rule derives `retired` after 2026-09-10) should cite that field, which turns the successor claim from a reading of the names into a quotation of the source.

### The price comparison gives only the axis where the successor is dearer

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260904-25-carry-2.md`.

The annotation compares "a prompt price of 0.000000075 against this row's 0.00000006" and stops. On completion the direction reverses and by more: `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash` is 0.00000025 against `z-ai/glm-4.7-flash`'s 0.0000004, both read from the same 2026-09-04 snapshot. So the successor is 25% dearer on input and 37.5% cheaper on output, and a reader shown only the first number is being pointed away from the migration the annotation is recommending. Adding the completion pair fixes it.

### An internal repository path reached visitor-facing prose

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260904-25-carry-3.md`.

The annotation renders on the home changed feed under the label "What it means" (`lib/render/home.mjs:48-57`), so "the registry note (data/sources/registry.json, status_rule) describes as reading active" is text a site visitor reads, pointing at a file they cannot open. Parsed every annotation in `data/changes.jsonl` and regex-scanned each `text` field for repo paths: of the eight, this is the only one that names one — the precedents say "this site's expiration-date rule" and leave the plumbing out (j-20260904-08, j-20260901-08, j-20260902-02). Naming a job id is established house style and fine; naming a source path is new. Dropping the parenthetical to "the far-future sentinel this site's status rule reads as active" loses nothing.

### Fix the stutter the product fact creates when transcluded

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260903-10-carry-2.md`.

The org body reads "The about page calls Mercury {{fact:org/inception-labs#product}}", and that fact's value is "diffusion-based large language models (dLLMs); it calls Mercury 'the world's first commercially available family of diffusion large language models'". renderFact (lib/facts.mjs:217) splices the value inline, so the rendered sentence says "calls Mercury ... it calls Mercury ..." twice in one clause. Dropping "; it calls Mercury" from the fact value, or rewriting the lead-in to "The about page describes", fixes it.

### Signal that the technologies enumeration is partial

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260903-10-carry-3.md`.

The org body presents the about page's research list as "the foundation line (Diffusion Models, Flash Attention, Direct Preference Optimization) and the discrete-diffusion line Mercury descends from (Masked Diffusion, Block Diffusion, Remasking Diffusion, and d1 Reasoning)". The page actually lists nine items; Discrete Diffusion Guidance (arxiv.org/abs/2412.10193) and Decision Transformers (arxiv.org/abs/2106.01345) are dropped without a word saying the enumeration is a selection. "among them" or a named omission would fix it.

The annotation closes "with the same rule deriving `retired` once 2026-09-10 passes." True of the rule's arithmetic, and every annotation of this shape has ended the same way — but the identical clause in j-20260901-08 ("the same rule derives `retired` once 2026-09-04 passes") is falsified today: nex-agi/nex-n2-mini and nex-n2-pro moved their date to 2026-09-08 on 2026-09-02 and are still active-listed on 2026-09-04. Because a date change with no status change emits no change record, the forecast quietly stops being true and nothing in the file says so. The clause should read as conditional on the date holding — one word, and it stops the log making predictions the same log later contradicts.

The five rows of the record's "Fixed" table are now correct and I verified each against lib/facts.mjs. Every figure in the two sections below it is not. Rendering each quoted line's transclusions through renderFact(..., { inline: true }) against data/derived gives: cohere-command-a.md:72 renders "256000 tokens context window", the record says 200000; meta-muse-glimmer-30b.md:98 renders "a 131072 tokens context window", the record says 1000000; inception-mercury-2-5-preview.md:128 renders "260000 tokens of context and a max output of 65536 tokens", the record says 1107 for both; qwen-qwen3-8-27b.md:77 renders "262144 tokens of context; this row lists 1000000 tokens", the record repeats 262144 for the second; x-ai-grok-4-6.md:110 renders "1000000 tokens of context at 0.00000125 USD per token input", the record says 0.0000008; z-ai-glm-5-1.md:80 renders 1048576, the record says 1000000; spacexai.md:71 renders 2000000, the record says 200000. The READINGS those figures annotate are all correct — my own corpus-wide sweep returns 0 suspects — so the record's auditable claim holds and nothing on the public site is affected; the quotes illustrating it were not read off a rendered page. The 1107 that appears twice is traceable: inception-mercury-2-5-preview.md:110 quotes the vendor's "achieving 1,107 tokens/sec on standard GPUs", a throughput claim inside a quotation, which the same record separately and wrongly calls "a currency-literal lint case" — it is neither a currency literal nor a context window. The gemini-3-8-flash docket attributes two things to https://9to5google.com/2026/09/02/gemini-3-8-flash-launch/ that I could not reproduce from that page with my own extractor: Wiz's "+7.5-9.7% recall" (the page as I retrieved it says only "higher recall on their internal penetration testing benchmark for a 2.3-5.2x lower cost", with no percentage range), and the sentence "At times, the model might use more tokens to maximize performance, especially at higher effort levels" (I retrieved the adjacent "works harder" framing as "exhibit[s] greater diligence — executing extra reasoning steps, and calling tools iteratively"). This is NOT a finding that either is wrong — WebFetch's extractor denies text that is present as readily as it invents text, so absence through it proves nothing, and every other figure in this docket reproduced exactly. It is a flag that these two are the only unconfirmed items in the set: the entry job that picks this candidate up should quote whichever sentence the page actually carries, and drop the percentage range if it is not there rather than carry it forward on the docket's authority.

The candidate's summary and why-now both say the site's own post "ends with the sentence 'Until the system card lands, the capability numbers are OpenAI's word.'" The candidate's evidence block quotes the release page's prose ("saturates FrontierMath Tier 4 with a 98% score") and its done-when line then lists "FrontierMath Tier 4 97.6/98" as if both were table rows. items.detail:
verify-daybreak-defense-network-product-wording.md says "a plain `user-agent`-only fetch returns HTTP 403 (Cloudflare challenge); the successful request sent `accept-language: en-US,en;q=0.9` and `cache-control: no-cache` alongside a full Chrome UA." That did not reproduce on 2026-09-04 from this machine: a fetch sending ONLY the same full Chrome `user-agent` returned HTTP 200 with 375,911 bytes, while a fetch sending no headers at all (Node's default UA) returned HTTP 403 with 9,861 bytes. So the header that clears the challenge is the UA alone; `accept-language` and `cache-control` were not load-bearing. The fix is to restate the note as "a fetch with no browser user-agent returns 403; sending a full Chrome UA returns 200", or to drop the causal claim and record only the headers that were sent. Nothing else in the file depends on this — the retrieval it describes reproduces exactly. Note that Cloudflare gating is IP- and time-dependent, so the author may well have observed the 403 they recorded; the note is unreliable as a general instrument claim rather than dishonest.

The underlying observation is real — that page's stripped length was 2556 in the transcript and 2548 when I fetched it myself minutes later — but as written the sentence describes a second fetch the transcript does not contain. Either capture both fetches, or say it plainly ("the page was fetched in both this run and the earlier one and rendered differently; only this run's is captured"). This is the same narrative-outruns-transcript shape the previous pass flagged, at much smaller scale, which is why it is carried rather than blocked on.
